```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Demand evidence for A is more direct and comes from multiple sources. Three separate Reddit posts show caregivers describing unresolved coordination pain, such as Google Sheets for medications and group texts not built for caregiving. B's demand rests on one LinkedIn comment plus a 'seed HN quote' that is referenced but never shown, so the HN quote counts as missing.",
    "Willingness to pay is better documented for A. Six live competitors publish consumer prices of $3.99–$7/mo, plus higher tiers up to $24.99/mo. One paying customer at that price point within 90 days is a low bar. B's price evidence points to enterprise-style buying, with Sendoso estimated at $15k–$20k+/yr. B's own brief calls this a poor match for a one-person self-serve build.",
    "A's product is software only. The brief notes that one- or two-person teams have already shipped comparable products. B's core risks are sourcing, warehousing, customs, breakage and address failures. The brief itself says these are physical-logistics problems that AI agents don't solve.",
    "A has a near-zero-cost channel for reaching its first customers. The brief shows caregivers on Reddit actively seeking app recommendations. B's channels are less proven for a first sale. The Stripe App Marketplace requires passing review first, and paid social is cited at $150–$250 per MQL/SQL for SaaS.",
    "A has serious problems: a crowded field, users who want it free, short customer lifetime, and activation that depends on siblings joining. These mostly limit how far A can scale. They block a first paying customer less than B's logistics and buyer-fit problems do."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's only shown demand signal is a single LinkedIn commenter asking which vendor Stripe used to send gifts. The commenter was a recipient expressing curiosity, not a founder saying they would pay for a Stripe-triggered swag tool. The brief admits this ('from someone receiving rather than needing to build it'). The 'seed HN quote' it builds on is never quoted, so it counts as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's evidence is stronger, but it has real holes. One of its three demand quotes explicitly says the app must be free, which undercuts paid conversion. The Meta CPC benchmark comes from a 2017 general source. The brief also names no differentiating wedge against six or more competitors. B could plausibly reach one higher-value B2B customer, but the briefs give no evidence that a solo-founder buyer exists for it."
}
```
